title: Policy-driven staged shadow-apply and rollback for batching & cache config changes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a policy-driven staged 'shadow-apply' workflow for applying batching and KV-cache configuration changes, combined with an automated rollback controller that reconciles applied state against expected safe-state and cost/latency feedback. Goal is to enable aggressive cost-saving recommendations to be safely evaluated and rolled back automatically if safety or SLO regressions are detected.

Scope:
- A staged apply mode: dry-run -> shadow (mirror traffic sampling + metric diff) -> live canary -> full rollout.
- Policy engine to declare safety criteria: latency p95 SLO, error rate delta, tail memory and GPU utilization, and cost-per-token improvement thresholds.
- Automated rollback controller that watches metrics, compares to policy limits, and performs either partial rollback (revert canary) or full rollback.
- State reconciliation: periodic audits that reconcile running node configs with control-plane intent, detect drift, and reapply safe baseline.
- Simulation harness to run config changes against historical traces to predict cost/latency trade-offs before apply.

Why this is different: Existing rollback work focuses on hard circuit-breakers and reconciler loops; this ticket adds a staged shadow-apply path with explicit cost-feedback loops and simulated validation that allow us to recommend and safely apply batching/caching profiles without manual ops intervention.

Out-of-scope: UI for console rollout creation (follow-up PM ticket), long-term ML-based anomaly detection (separate research initiative).
acceptance_criteria: Shadow-apply mode implemented: config changes can be applied in shadow for at least 5% of traffic with no impact to live responses
Policy engine accepts rules for latency p95, error-rate delta, GPU memory delta, and cost-per-token delta
Controller automatically reverts canary if any policy threshold is breached within the monitoring window
Reconciliation job detects drift for >= 95% of intentionally-paused nodes and re-syncs them to the baseline within 2 minutes
Simulation harness produces a cost/latency delta report for a given config change within 10 minutes and synthetic-verifies rollout policy
E2E integration tests and a staging run demonstrating an automated rollback triggered by a simulated latency spike
comments: 2025-02-10 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after cost-savings spike experiment caused unexpected tail latency increases in staging. Attached design notes: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1DesignDocShadowApply

2025-02-11 - Mateo Ruiz: Initial architecture sketch uploaded to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124. Key components: ShadowProxy, PolicyEvaluator, RollbackOrchestrator, Reconciler

2025-02-12 - Performance: Ran a 24h historical trace simulation comparing current batching profile vs recommended aggressive profile. Result: 22% token-cost reduction but 14ms p95 regression on long-sequence workloads (details in simulation report).

2025-02-13 - Eng sync: Agreed to require simulation pass (cost improvement >= 10% and p95 regression <= 5ms) before proceeding to canary. Added hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping during transient noise.
2025-02-14 - Design review (PM/Platform): PM requested dashboard hooks for rollouts and a 'freeze' label to exclude customer-critical routes. Added label handling in PolicyEvaluator.
2025-02-15 - PR feedback: @liangchen requested adding circuit-breaker state persistance for cross-node rollback coordination. Will add checkpointing to RollbackOrchestrator.
2025-02-16 - Safety review kickoff: Submitted checklist to security for KMS access and audit-log requirements: https://confluence.redwood.ai/safety/shadow-apply

2025-02-17 - Mateo Ruiz: Implemented shadow traffic splitter and metric diff reporter. Canary rollback tested in staging; triggered correctly when synthetic latency injected. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3189

2025-02-18 - QA: Running full-suite E2E in staging; found a race when multiple concurrent config changes apply — added global operation sequencer as mitigation. Next: add reconciliation unit tests and schedule canary run against production-like traffic sample on 2025-02-24.
